mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that lead to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 5% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5pp does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals a strong supply-side recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO rise > 2% does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson's r < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) growth is below 2%, the combination signals a disinflationary environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY < 2% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase > 300,000 does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson's r < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts (HOUST) and falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises and UNRATE falls in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of rising HOUST and falling UNRATE does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson's r < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative growth for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 negative growth for 2 quarters does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.1).
